title: Deep Interest Network for Click-Through Rate Prediction
grouping: Three parts in a row: 'Base Model' at left and 'Deep Interest Network' at centre, each with a bold caption beneath, and a double-outlined panel at upper right showing the inside of one Activation Unit, with a legend below it. Inputs are grouped by curly braces into labelled feature fields along the bottom: User Profile Features, User Behaviors (Goods 1 … Goods N), Candidate Ad, Context Features; a large brace above the concatenated features gathers them into the MLP.
shapes_depth: Each input ID is a small coloured circle at the bottom (Goods ID orange-red, Shop ID blue, Cate ID pink, Other ID white); each becomes a short vertical bar of cells in the same colour family, then a small rounded 'Concat' box and a horizontal multi-colour vector strip. The MLP layers are wide light-grey flat bars labelled in a monospace font (PReLU (200), PReLU (80), Softmax (2), Output). Activation Units are double-outlined rounded boxes; their weights multiply in through pink circled 'X' product glyphs. Grey and black thin arrows; no shadows.
proposed_highlight: The proposed network sits beside the base model with exactly the same input row and MLP stack, so the inserted Activation Units and pink product glyphs over the behaviour sequence are the only new parts; the unit's internals are expanded in a double-bordered detail panel whose border matches the units' double outline.
lesson: Draw each input feature field as a coloured ID dot whose colour carries into its embedding cells, so the concatenated vectors further up visibly show which fields they mix and one small legend of dot colours explains the whole input side.
notes: year = arXiv preprint year (1706.06978); venue KDD from Semantic Scholar (venue_source: semantic-scholar), the PDF's first page states no venue. elements 'other' = the multi-colour concatenated embedding strips.

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)

taxonomy.note: architecture other = target attention: a candidate-ad-conditioned attention pooling over user behaviour embeddings

insights.structure: Base Model on the left and Deep Interest Network in the middle share the same bottom-up skeleton (feature groups -> embeddings -> pooling -> concat -> MLP), with a double-bordered inset at top right expanding the Activation Unit.
insights.data: IDs are coloured circles (orange goods, blue shop, pink category, white other), embeddings are short multi-coloured vertical strips, pooled vectors are horizontal coloured cell bars, and FC layers are grey labelled boxes ('PReLU (200)').
insights.emphasis: DIN's change is the row of double-bordered Activation Unit boxes, each emitting a 'Goods i Weight' into a red X product circle before SUM Pooling, fed by a line from the candidate ad; the rest is identical to the base model so the difference pops.
insights.flow: Bottom to top in both models; the candidate ad embedding runs horizontally under the activation units to every behaviour, and the user-profile/context branches go straight up to Concat & Flatten.
insights.avoid: Small text and a dense tangle of thin grey arrows around the activation units make the middle panel hard to read at column width.

arrangement.units: Two unframed model panels (Base Model, Deep Interest Network, titled at the bottom) plus a double-bordered inset detailing the Activation Unit.
arrangement.inputs_as: coloured ID circles grouped by feature field (User Profile, User Behaviors Goods 1..N, Candidate Ad, Context)
arrangement.losses_at: none drawn; Output box at the top
arrangement.shared: the embedding layer and MLP tower drawn identically in both panels
